title: She Took a WPL Hat-Trick in Her Second Match. Five Weeks Later, She Made Her India Debut. Now She's Going to the World Cup.
excerpt: Nandni Sharma's rise from Chandigarh's boys' academies to India's T20 World Cup squad is the fastest ascent in Indian women's cricket this year
body:
She grew up in Chandigarh, watching her elder brother head to the cricket ground every morning. At eight, she joined an academy. She trained alongside boys because there weren't enough girls to form a proper side. She briefly stepped away when opportunities dried up, then came back harder.

Nandani Sharma — Nandni, as she prefers — is 24 years old, a right-arm fast-medium bowler, and until five weeks ago, she had never represented India in any format. On May 28, in Chelmsford, she walked out for her T20I debut against England and took three wickets for 34 runs.

On June 14, she will be part of the squad that faces Pakistan at Edgbaston in the opening match of the ICC Women's T20 World Cup.

## From WPL Hat-Trick to National Colours

The breakthrough arrived this year, in the Women's Premier League. Delhi Capitals picked her up for INR 20 lakh — a modest sum by WPL standards, but enough to validate years of domestic grind. In her second WPL appearance, she produced a performance that made selectors sit up: five wickets for 33 runs against Gujarat Giants, including a hat-trick. She became the first uncapped Indian to take a WPL hat-trick and only the second Indian player to register a five-wicket haul in the competition.

By the end of the tournament, she had 17 wickets in 10 matches at an average of 18.58 — joint-highest in WPL 2026 alongside Sophie Devine. The pace wasn't express, but the control was relentless. She struck in powerplays. She struck at the death. She mixed seam with slower balls, the kind of versatility that doesn't come from raw talent alone.

When the BCCI announced the 15-player World Cup squad on May 2, her name was there. Amanjot Kaur's injury and Kashvee Gautam's knee problem had opened the door, but Nandni had kicked it wide open.

## Debut at Chelmsford — A Statement, Not a Fluke

The India tour of England before the World Cup was designed as a dress rehearsal. In the first T20I at Chelmsford on May 28, Nandni made her international debut and immediately justified her selection. Her three wickets for 34 helped India win by 38 runs, the visitors' most comprehensive result of the series.

India went on to lose the T20I series 1-2, with England's Alice Capsey (82 off 43 balls) and Heather Knight (70 not out off 42) dismantling them in the deciding third match at Taunton. But Harmanpreet Kaur, who made an unbeaten 56 in that game, remained composed afterward.

"Lot of positives going into the World Cup," Harmanpreet said. "We are pretty clear. We have two more practice games before the World Cup. We can think about combinations, but we are pretty clear on the XI going forward."

## What India Carry Into England

The squad is familiar: Harmanpreet leads for the fifth time in a T20 World Cup. Smriti Mandhana is vice-captain. Shafali Verma, Jemimah Rodrigues, and Richa Ghosh form the batting core. Deepti Sharma, Shreyanka Patil, Radha Yadav, and Shree Charani provide spin options. Renuka Thakur and Arundhati Reddy are the pace pillars.

But the squad's form is not without concern. Since the 2024 T20 World Cup, India have won 13 of 21 T20Is. This year, the record is starker: three wins in eight matches, including four losses in the five-match series against South Africa.

The reigning ODI World Cup champions know that the T20 format has been less kind. India have never won a Women's T20 World Cup. The closest they came was in 2020, when they made the final at the MCG against Australia.

## The Diaspora Angle

For NRI cricket fans who followed the men's team dominating Afghanistan in Mullanpur this weekend, the women's World Cup offers a different kind of intensity. The tournament begins June 12 in England and runs until July 5. India's group includes Pakistan (June 14, Edgbaston), Netherlands (June 17, Headingley), South Africa (June 21, Old Trafford), Bangladesh (June 25, Old Trafford), and the mammoth clash against Australia (June 28, Lord's).

In the US and Canada, all matches will be available free on Willow Sports. In India, Star Sports and JioHotstar carry every game.

The World Cup is in England, in English summer conditions — seaming pitches, overcast skies, swing bowling. India's pace unit will be tested. And somewhere in that unit, a 24-year-old from Chandigarh who was training with boys four years ago will be running in to bowl.

Her name is Nandni Sharma. Remember it.
